text:
alex: quick heads-up — saw a host-side tail regression on the canary after the recent kernel-chooser tweak. p95 for short prompts (8-32 tokens) jumped ~18ms.

alex: traced it to the preparse chain + grpc smallwrite noise. flame shows a lot more syscalls during the initial tokenization/parse phase.

maria: can you paste the logs/pprof snapshot?

alex: here's the condensed pprof top (host parse region):
```
HostParse_CopyBytes  23.4%  23.4%  1.8s
gRPC_SmallWrite_Syscall  18.9%  42.3%  1.45s
Tokenize_Normalize  15.2%  57.5%  1.16s
KVCache_Lookup  9.3%  66.8%  0.71s
Batching_StickyWindow  4.1% 70.9%  0.31s
```

alex: also saw kvcache miss-rate spike ~2.3x during bursts, which increases backend work.

lee: remind me — what did the kernel chooser change do?

alex: chooser started preferring the new fused-attn FP16 kernel for sequences < 64. that kernel expects pre-normalized input, so we added a host-side normalize pass to be safe. that extra pass copies bytes and creates more small write frames into the proxy.

jia: smallwrites are awful for HPACK + http2 headroom. we should try coalescing at the proxy layer (writev) as a quick mitigation.

maria: did you try a canary with coalescing?

alex: yes — toggled writev/coalesce on the grpc proxy in a canary. config diff: 
```
# grpc-proxy.conf
small_write_coalesce_bytes: 4096
writev_enabled: true
writev_batch_limit: 8
```

alex: results after 30m: syscalls down ~38%, host-parse p95 down ~12ms, kv-miss down ~10% (probably because fewer fragmented frames = better KV shard locality).

lee: nice. that explains part of it. kvcache thrash still present though?

alex: yes — kvcache eviction rate still higher than baseline during very bursty fanout. suspect key canonicalization variance + frame fragmentation causing uneven shard keys.

jia: two-pronged: (1) short-term proxy coalesce + writev (done in canary), (2) medium-term canonicalize KV keys on host before lookup + reduce per-request metadata in key.

maria: batching heuristics angle: can we make batch windows sticky for repeated sessions (same user) to increase batch hit rate for short sequences without raising latency for first token? e.g., 10ms sticky for active session.

lee: re: kernel chooser, we can add an opt-in flag per-model that says "model-accepts-raw-tokens" to skip host normalize for models we onboarded. that'll avoid the copy for most open models.

alex: performance numbers on canary v2 (30m window):
- p50: -1ms
- p95: -12ms
- host CPU parse region: -7%
- syscalls: -38%
- kvcache miss-rate: -10%

alex: no regressions on long sequences up to 1024; throughput dip ~2% (expected trade).

deploy-bot: canary token-shear-coalesce v2 deployed -> 2026-03-22T18:12:00Z

jia: i'll own the writev test + unit coverage. will push PR with a toggle and some benchmarks.

lee: i'll start the kvcache canonicalization PR and add telemetry to track shard fanout per key.

alex: i'll add the chooser flag and a small integration test to ensure skipping normalize is safe. also add a microbench for short sequence path.

maria: action items summary: 1) land grpc proxy writev/coalesce (jia) 2) kvcache canonicalization + shard telemetry (lee) 3) chooser per-model flag to skip normalize (alex) 4) sticky-batching experiment (maria/alex)

maria: also add a follow-up postmortem if the canary unearths any new regressions. :thumbsup:

lee: taking the kvcache work — will ping when draft PR is up.

jia: drafting writev PR now, will link perf run.

alex: i left a short perf-run script in the canary channel; run it locally if you want numbers. thanks all.

maria: great progress. keep the canary open for 2h and then roll to stable if no issues.

alex: noted.
